chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ali ibn Salim from Yahya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who had intercourse with his female slave unlawfully, then bought her and claimed her son as his. He said: He said, 'He is not inherited from him, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and to the fornicator is the stone.' And the child of fornication is not inherited except by a man who claims the son of his female slave.'

17 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari who said: Some of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) with me, asking him about a man who had intercourse with a woman unlawfully, then he married her after pregnancy, and she brought forth a child who was most similar in creation to him. He wrote (peace be upon him) in his own hand and with his seal: 'The child belongs to the one who had intercourse unlawfully; he is not inherited.'

key_terms.الْحَجَر: The stone (symbolizing the share or right)
key_terms.الْفِرَاش: The bed (referring to the father's marital bed)
key_terms.غَيَّة: A specific term here referring to the one who had intercourse

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a child born from a master's unlawful intercourse with his own slave girl?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance status of a son born from unlawful intercourse (*Zina*) with a female slave (*Umm Walad*) before her purchase, ruling that he does not inherit from the father despite the man's claim. The text reinforces the principle of *Al-Walad lil-Firash* (the child belongs to the bed/marital bed) and distinguishes this from the specific case of *Zina* where the child is not inherited unless the father explicitly acknowledges him, as noted in the second report by Imam al-Sadiq. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on lineage purity and the distinction between *Nasab* (lineage) and inheritance rights in cases of concubinage versus marriage.
